chunks: And through his chain of narration from Abi Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah – or [and] Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) – say: Whoever loves that his dwelling and abode be Paradise, let him not neglect the Ziyarah of the oppressed one.
I asked, "And who is he?" He replied: Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), the master of Karbala.

Whoever goes to him with yearning for him, and love for the Messenger of Allah, and love for the Commander of the Believers, and love for Fatimah, Allah will seat him at the tables of Paradise, eating with them while the people are undergoing the reckoning.

key_terms.الْمَظْلُوم: The oppressed one (specifically referring to Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Ziyarah (visitation/pilgrimage to the shrine of an Imam or saint)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ كَرْبَلَاءَ: The master/companion of Karbala (referring to Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.مَوَائِدِ الْجَنَّة: Tables of Paradise (a metaphor for high status and sustenance in the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) with love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) linking the spiritual status of the visitor directly to the specific love for the Ahl al-Bayt, identifying Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as the ultimate 'oppressed' whose Ziyarah guarantees a seat at the tables of Paradise. This hadith emphasizes that such devotion elevates the believer above the general crowd during the intense scrutiny of the Day of Judgment, highlighting the intercessory and salvific power of the Imams' suffering.
